newsitem.title: UK: Taylor Woodrow sees promising H2 start.
newsitem.headline: Taylor Woodrow sees promising H2 start.

text.p: Taylor Woodrow, the building to property development group, reported a rosy start to the second half on Tuesday after unveiling an 81 percent leap in first half pretax profits to 25.4 million pounds ($39.4 million).
Colin Parsons, group chairman, said in the interim results statement: "Taylor Woodrow has had a good first half in 1996 and progress in the second half of the year to date is most encouraging."
The profit surge for the six months ended June 30 was attributed to improved performances across all group divisions.

The company also took the opportunity to announce that group chief executive Tony Palmer will retire in June 1997 and that a successor is being sought. An appointment is expected before full year results next March.
The latest half year group sales were up to 556.4 million stg from 547.4 million. The interim dividend was raised to 1.0 pence from 0.75 pence per share.
The chairman also reported "substantial improvements in the profitability of operations in the UK and USA." ($1=.6444 Pound)
